title: Epic — Silkweb v1: rebuild MWeb core with real folder structuring
description:
## Summary

Silkweb is a clean-room native macOS offline Markdown library and editor (macOS 15+, SwiftUI + AppKit) that rebuilds MWeb’s core writing experience while fixing the main gap: **one unified library where nested folders on disk own documents** (UTF-8 `.md`), with tags/search/editing in one place—not separate category DB vs Folders modes.

This epic tracks the **Core v1** sequence from `research.md` (2026-10-01): durable storage and folder mutations first, then shell and editing, preview/rendering, search/tags, export, and polish. The repo today is a skeleton (version constant + placeholder window); no feature code to preserve.

**Principles:** offline-first, no accounts/backend; atomic saves; macOS Trash for deletion; versioned tolerant JSON metadata; performance targets 10k docs / 1k folders with work off the main thread; keyboard-friendly native Mac UX.

**Build/test gate:** `./scripts/build.sh` and `./scripts/build.sh test` per issue; no bare `swift build`. QA PASS + Orchestrator approval closes issues on `team/roadmap`.

**Existing open issues:** None at research time (no prior `.beads`); no duplicates noted.

## Open questions (defaults apply until answered)

1. Is the pain specifically MWeb Library categories, or a failing operation in its Folders window? The proposed unified model addresses the former without falsely claiming MWeb lacks the latter.
2. Is the proposed Core release sufficient without math/Mermaid, full CommonMark conformance, tabs, focus/typewriter and DOCX/ePub? Which is a daily necessity?
3. Should the initial library open an existing directory in place by default, or start with a new folder and offer Import Copy? Both should remain explicit.
4. Are sidecar tags acceptable, or must tags travel inside Markdown front matter? The proposal avoids altering document text; a portable front-matter contract is separate scope.
5. Confirm system Trash plus Finder restoration for v1, direct folder counts, and name/date sorting without manual order.
6. Is migration via MWeb's own Markdown folder export sufficient? Multiple category memberships can become duplicate exported files; automated DB migration would require a separate clean-room specification.
7. Does switching to standard Cmd-O and Cmd-Shift-O matter more than copying MWeb's contextual Cmd-O behavior?

## Out of scope for this epic

Follow-up issues required (not in the 25 Core tickets): **Math**, **Mermaid**, **full CommonMark conformance**, **tabs/session**, **focus/typewriter**, **backups/history UI**, **HTML paste conversion**, **TextBundle**, **rich text copy**, **DOCX**, and **ePub**. Also excluded: online publishing, image hosting, static-site generation, CloudKit/sync, mobile apps, script/Pandoc auto-execution, manual document ordering on disk, scroll-synced preview, backlink browser, Quick Note, pin/unpin, and proprietary MWeb image-width syntax as default.

No third-party dependency is silently assumed; math/diagrams need explicitly scoped follow-ups with approved dependencies.

(2) Tags are stored in the Silkweb sidecar index (.silkweb metadata) — never written into .md text/front matter. (3) First launch offers BOTH 'Open folder in place' and 'New library'; 'Import Copy' lives in the File menu.

(5) Tab bar appears only with 2+ tabs (Safari-style). (6) Cmd+/Cmd- is per-window temporary zoom; Settings holds the base size. (7) Word count = Markdown source with markup stripped. (8) Shortcut map in docs/design-system.md is the source of truth (Ctrl-Cmd-M Move To, Opt-Cmd-R Reveal in Finder, Shift-Cmd-I Import Folder Copy, Ctrl-Cmd-T Insert Table, Ctrl-Shift-Cmd-F/T Focus/Typewriter, Opt-Cmd-1..3 pane focus; Cmd-1..9 not used for tabs). title: #1 Disk library model and tolerant metadata
description:
**Roadmap #:** 1 · **Scope:** L · **Priority:** P1

### User problem
Notes need a durable, tool-independent home on disk.

### Proposed behavior
Enumerate one library root into folder/document models off the main thread; UTF-8 reads; stable app IDs; versioned JSON with tolerant decode and rebuildable derived index; no implicit symlink traversal.

### MWeb / competitor reference
Library files plus category database (Silkweb: real folders + `.md` + versioned JSON index).

### Likely files
Sources/SilkwebCore/LibraryModels.swift, LibraryScanner.swift, LibraryMetadata.swift; Tests/SilkwebCoreTests/LibraryScannerTests.swift (or similar).

### Constraints
Persistence: version JSON; missing keys default safely; bodies stay in `.md` only. Performance: enumeration off main thread; target 10k/1k synthetic tree.
design:
## UX notes — silkweb-1.1 Disk library model (Core-only)
Foundation: `.team/ux/_design-system.md` (vocabulary §2). There is no UI in this ticket. These notes define names and states the app layer (1.4) will display, so the Core API should expose them.

**Naming in the model/API:** `Library` (root), `Folder`, `Document`. Never "Category" or "Note". The root folder's display name is the directory name. `displayName` for a document is the filename without the `.md`/`.markdown` extension. Keep the real filename separately for Finder-related copy.

**Scan states the UI needs** (expose as an enum/progress, not strings):
- `loading(progress: scannedCount)`: 1.4 shows "Loading library…" with a count after 1 s ("Loading library… 4,210 documents").
- `loaded`.
- `rootMissing`: 1.4 shows "Library Not Found".
- `permissionDenied`: "Silkweb doesn’t have permission to read “<name>”."
- `notADirectory`.

**Recoverable conditions** to surface as non-blocking info, not errors:
- `metadataRecovered(backupURL)`: malformed index set aside. The app may show a one-time Editor Banner–style notice in the sidebar footer: "Silkweb rebuilt its library index. The previous index was kept as “<file>”." No alert, no action required.
- `skippedSymlinks(count)` and `unreadableItems([relativePath])`: shown later in Library info. The UI ignores them for v1, but keep the data.

**Error copy hooks** (`LocalizedError.errorDescription` / `recoverySuggestion`):
- Missing root: "Silkweb can’t find the library “<name>”." / "It may have been moved, renamed, or be on a disconnected drive."
- Permission: "Silkweb doesn’t have permission to read “<name>”." / "Choose the folder again to grant access."
- Non-UTF-8 document: flag the document `isReadOnlyEncoding`. 1.5 opens it read-only with a banner. Don't fail the scan.

**Ordering:** return children unsorted or by natural order (`localizedStandardCompare`). 1.9 owns presentation order.

**Reserved names:** `.silkweb` and `.silkweb-assets` are hidden. Export the reserved-name list as a public constant, because 1.6's rename validation reuses it.

**Out of scope:** any UI, sort preferences, counts presentation.

title: #10 Copy-import of a Markdown folder
description:
**Roadmap #:** 10 · **Scope:** M · **Priority:** P1

### User problem
Existing Markdown trees cannot enter the managed workflow safely.

### Proposed behavior
Preview import plan; copy nested structure and empty directories; copy supported local assets; reject silent replacement; report external/unsupported references; source directory untouched.

### MWeb / competitor reference
Folder import with local images.

### Likely files
Sources/SilkwebCore/ImportPlan.swift, FolderImporter.swift; Sources/Silkweb/ImportSheet.swift.

### Constraints
Never overwrite destination silently; detect references outside import root.
design:
## UX notes — silkweb-1.10 Copy-import of a Markdown folder
Foundation: `.team/ux/_design-system.md` (§2 naming: **Import Folder Copy…**; §5.4 Folder Picker; §6: ⇧⌘I). Owner decision: Import Copy lives in the **File menu** only. It isn't on the Welcome screen, which only mentions it as a hint. It's disabled when no library is open.

### Flow
1. **File ▸ Import Folder Copy… ⇧⌘I** opens an `NSOpenPanel` (directories only, prompt "Choose") with the message "Choose a folder of Markdown files to copy into your library. The original folder won’t be changed."
2. **Destination:** the target folder per the 1.6 target rule. The plan sheet shows it with a **Change…** button that opens the shared Folder Picker (1.7) titled "Import Into…" with button "Choose".
3. **Review (plan sheet).** Scanning happens off-main. After 300 ms, show "Reviewing “Research Notes”…" with an indeterminate progress bar and **Cancel**.
4. **Plan sheet**, 540×560:
```
Import “Research Notes”
Copy into:  [folder] Writing   [Change…]

  128 documents, 34 images, 12 folders (3 empty) will be copied
  into a new folder “Research Notes”.

  ▸ Will be renamed (2)
  ▸ Won’t be copied (5)
  ▸ Links outside the folder (3)

                                    [Cancel]  [Import]
```
   - The import always creates **one new folder** named after the source inside the destination. If that name is taken, the summary says: "“Research Notes” already exists here, so the copy will be named “Research Notes 2”." Never merge into an existing folder.
   - **Will be renamed**: in-source case-insensitive duplicates and invalid names. Rows: "notes.md → notes 2.md".
   - **Won’t be copied**: rows show the relative path plus a reason: "Not a Markdown document or a linked image", "Hidden item", "Symbolic link", "Couldn’t be read".
   - **Links outside the folder**: "document › link". Footnote: "These files won’t be copied. The links stay as written."
   - Disclosure groups start collapsed and show counts. Each list caps at 200 rows with "and 57 more".
   - Images and attachments referenced by imported documents and located under the source root are copied to keep relative links working. Unreferenced images are listed under "Won’t be copied".
5. **Import** (default; Return) shows a determinate progress state in the same sheet: "Copying 54 of 128 documents…" with **Stop**. Copying goes to a staging location and moves into place at the end, so **Stop** leaves nothing behind. Stop asks no question: "Import stopped. Nothing was added to your library." Button **OK**.
6. **Done:** the sheet closes. The sidebar expands the destination and selects the new folder, and the list shows its documents. There's no success alert, since the result is visible.

### States and errors
| Case | Copy |
|---|---|
| No Markdown files | title "No Markdown documents found", body "“X” doesn’t contain any .md or .markdown files." **Import** disabled; only **Cancel** |
| Source is inside this library | alert "This folder is already in your library." / "Use Move To… to reorganize it instead." |
| Library is inside source | alert "You can’t import a folder that contains your library." |
| Unreadable source | "Silkweb can’t read “X”." / reason |
| Disk full or copy failure | "The import couldn’t be completed." / reason + "Nothing was added to your library." |

The source folder is never modified (no metadata written into it).

### Accessibility
Disclosure groups are labeled with their counts ("Won’t be copied, 5 items"). Progress is announced at start and end. All controls are reachable by keyboard (Tab order: Change… → disclosure groups → Cancel → Import).

### Out of scope
Drag-from-Finder import (follow-up), merging into existing folders, importing non-Markdown formats, MWeb database migration, watching the source for updates.

title: #11 Reconcile Finder changes and preserve conflicts
description:
**Roadmap #:** 11 · **Scope:** L · **Priority:** P1

### User problem
Files change outside Silkweb while the app is open.

### Proposed behavior
Filesystem notifications plus debounced background rescan; reload clean buffers; dirty conflicts keep both versions; external deletes detected without discarding drafts.

### MWeb / competitor reference
External folder workflow (exact conflict policy U).

### Likely files
Sources/SilkwebCore/LibraryReconciler.swift; Sources/Silkweb/LibraryWatcher.swift, ConflictSheet.swift.

### Constraints
No symlink cycle traversal; do not follow paths outside library root.
design:
## UX notes — silkweb-1.11 Reconcile Finder changes and preserve conflicts
Foundation: `.team/ux/_design-system.md` (§5.2 Editor Banner, §5.5 Alerts). Guiding rule: external changes are **quiet when safe** and **explicit when text could be lost**. Silkweb never discards either version.

### Silent cases (no UI beyond the update)
- Files or folders created, renamed, moved or deleted in Finder: the sidebar and list update after the debounced rescan without collapsing expansion or losing selection. If the selected folder disappears, select its parent. Batches of more than 20 changes apply without row animation.
- An open **clean** document changed on disk: reload in place. Keep the caret and scroll position (clamp the selection to the new length). Undo history resets.
- An open document moved or renamed externally and resolved by ID: the editor follows, and the title and path update.

### Conflict: open document is dirty and changed on disk
1. Pause autosave for that document immediately.
2. Show an Editor Banner (systemOrange `exclamationmark.triangle.fill`): "“plan” was changed outside Silkweb while you were editing." Buttons: **Compare…**, **Keep My Version**, **Use Disk Version**. There's no ✕, because the conflict must be resolved. Editing may continue meanwhile.
3. **Keep My Version:** write the buffer to `plan.md`. Save the disk version beside it as **"plan (Conflict 2026-10-01 10.42).md"** (`uniqueName` from 1.2 if needed).
4. **Use Disk Version:** load the disk text into the editor. Save the buffer as the conflict copy instead.
5. Either way, a follow-up info banner reads "The other version was saved as “plan (Conflict 2026-10-01 10.42)”." with a **Show** button (selects it in the list) and ✕.
6. **Compare… sheet** (`ConflictSheet`, 760×520): two read-only monospaced panes side by side, headed "Your Version (not saved)" and "Version on Disk · modified 10:42 AM". Panes scroll in sync. No diff coloring in v1. Buttons: **Cancel**, **Use Disk Version**, **Keep My Version** (default). Escape = Cancel, returning to the banner.

Conflict-copy naming must not contain `:` or `/`, which is why the time uses `HH.mm`.

### Open document deleted or trashed externally
- Banner: "“plan” was moved to the Trash or deleted outside Silkweb." Buttons: **Save Again** (recreate at the original path, or a unique name if it's taken) and **Close**. The buffer is kept regardless of dirty state, and autosave is paused until the user chooses.
- **Close** on a dirty buffer asks: "Close without saving “plan”?" / "Your changes will be lost." with **Cancel** (default) and **Close** (destructive).

### Folder-level cases
- Selected folder trashed externally: select its parent. No alert.
- Library root disappears: switch to the 1.4 "Library Not Found" window state. Open dirty buffers are written to recovery drafts (1.3) first.

### Banner priority (one at a time)
Conflict > external delete > save failure (1.5) > info.

### Accessibility
Every banner posts an announcement. Compare panes are labeled "Your version" and "Version on disk". All actions are keyboard reachable (Tab into the banner; banner buttons have no shortcuts).

### Out of scope
Three-way merge or diff highlighting, conflict history UI, reconciling metadata conflicts in tags (1.21 handles by ID).

title: #12 Markdown styling and formatting commands
description:
**Roadmap #:** 12 · **Scope:** L · **Priority:** P1

### User problem
Plain text editing lacks core Markdown writing assistance.

### Proposed behavior
Incremental heading/emphasis/code/link styling in editor; selection-safe bold, italic, strike, heading, quote, list, link, code commands; list continuation and indent/outdent.

### MWeb / competitor reference
Syntax menu and toolbar formatting assists.

### Likely files
Sources/SilkwebCore/MarkdownEditing.swift, MarkdownTokens.swift; Sources/Silkweb/MarkdownTextView.swift, FormatCommands.swift.

### Constraints
No full language syntax highlighter; respect IME and undo grouping.
design:
## UX notes — silkweb-1.12 Markdown styling and formatting commands
Foundation: `.team/ux/_design-system.md` (§4 colors, §6 Format menu row: all shortcuts are fixed there; use them exactly). This adds a **Format** menu between Edit and View. Every item is disabled unless the editor is first responder and editable.

### Format menu (order)
Bold ⌘B · Italic ⌘I · Strikethrough ⇧⌘X · Inline Code ⌃⌘C · — · Link ⌘K · Image… ⌃⌘I (added by 1.15) · — · Heading ▸ (Heading 1–6 ⌃⌘1–⌃⌘6, Body Text ⌃⌘0) · — · Quote ⌘' · Bulleted List ⌥⌘U · Numbered List ⌥⌘O · Task List ⌥⌘X · Code Block ⌃⇧⌘C · — · Shift Right ⌘] · Shift Left ⌘[ · — · Insert Table… ⌃⌘T (added by 1.14). The editor's context menu gets a "Format" submenu with the same items.
**No formatting toolbar in v1.** The editor chrome stays clean. *(Orchestrator: confirm.)*

### Command behavior
- **Inline wraps (bold `**`, italic `*`, strike `~~`, code `` ` ``):** a selection gets wrapped, or unwrapped if it's already wrapped, including when the markers sit just outside the selection. With an empty caret inside a word, wrap that word. With an empty caret elsewhere, insert the pair and put the caret between (`**|**`). Never split a grapheme cluster or an IME marked range. Commands are ignored while `hasMarkedText()`.
- **Link ⌘K:** wraps the selection as `[sel](|)` with the caret in the parentheses. If the clipboard holds an http(s) URL, insert it and place the caret after `)`. With no selection, insert `[](url)` with the caret in the brackets. No dialog.
- **Line commands (heading, quote, lists, code block)** act on every line touched by the selection. Headings replace any existing `#` prefix. The same level again toggles to body text. Lists toggle their marker. Numbered List numbers 1., 2., 3. Code Block wraps the lines in ``` fences and places the caret after the opening fence for the language.
- **Undo:** each command is one undo group with an action name: "Undo Bold", "Undo Heading", "Undo Bulleted List", and so on.

### List continuation and indentation
- Return in a list item continues the marker: `- ` / `* ` / `+ `, `3. ` → `4. `, `- [x] ` → `- [ ] `, keeping indentation. Return on an **empty** item removes the marker (ends the list). ⇧Return inserts a plain line break with no marker.
- Tab / ⇧Tab inside a list item = Shift Right / Left. Elsewhere Tab inserts the indent unit. ⌘] / ⌘[ work everywhere on the touched lines. The indent unit comes from settings (1.24; default 4 spaces).

### Live styling (attributes only; never alters text)
| Element | Style |
|---|---|
| Markers `#` `*` `_` `~~` `` ` `` `>` list bullets, `[ ]` | `tertiaryLabelColor` (kept visible; no hiding/WYSIWYG) |
| H1 / H2 / H3 / H4–H6 | semibold at 1.6× / 1.35× / 1.15× / 1.0× base size |

description:
**Roadmap #:** 13 · **Scope:** S · **Priority:** P1

### User problem
Long documents are hard to revise efficiently.

### Proposed behavior

### MWeb / competitor reference

design:
## UX notes — silkweb-1.13 Find and replace in a document
Foundation: `.team/ux/_design-system.md` (§6 Edit ▸ Find row). Use the **native `NSTextFinder` find bar** as-is. Don't restyle it or build a custom panel.

### Entry points (Edit ▸ Find submenu, standard order)
Find… ⌘F · Find and Replace… ⌥⌘F · Find Next ⌘G · Find Previous ⇧⌘G · Use Selection for Find ⌘E · Jump to Selection ⌘J. 1.20 appends **Search Library… ⇧⌘F** after a separator in the same submenu, so the two scopes sit next to each other with distinct names.

### Placement and behavior
- `usesFindBar = true`, `isIncrementalSearchingEnabled = true`. The bar appears at the top of the editor scroll view, under the tab bar and any Editor Banner, and pushes content down rather than overlaying it.
- With a selection, ⌘F pre-fills the selected text (system behavior). All matches get the incremental highlight. The current match is scrolled to about a third from the top.
- Escape or the bar's Done closes it, returns focus to the text view, and leaves the current match selected.
- **Replace / Replace All** are undoable. Replace All is a single undo group named "Undo Replace All".
- Focus: typing in the find field doesn't move the editor caret until Return / Find Next. After closing, focus always returns to the editor (acceptance: find never permanently steals focus).

### Enablement
| Context | Find items |
|---|---|
| Editor visible (Editor or Split mode) | enabled; acts on the editor |
| Sidebar or list focused with a document open | ⌘F moves focus to the editor and opens the bar |
| Preview-only mode (1.18) | disabled. Find in rendered preview is out of scope; ⌘R back to the editor |
| No document | disabled |
| Read-only document | Find enabled, Replace disabled |

### Interplay
- Focus Mode (1.27): jumping to a match moves the caret, so the focused paragraph follows. No special casing needed.
- Typewriter Mode: matches scroll to the typewriter anchor instead of the top third.
- Opening a document from Search Library results (1.20) pre-fills the find pasteboard with the query, so ⌘G jumps to the next hit.

### Accessibility
The native bar is fully accessible. Don't add custom views to it.

### Out of scope
Regex UI beyond what `NSTextFinder` offers, find in the preview, multi-document replace.

description:
**Roadmap #:** 14 · **Scope:** S · **Priority:** P2

### User problem
Hand-typing table scaffolding is tedious.

### Proposed behavior
User chooses rows, columns, alignment; insert valid pipe-table source as one undo action; bounded dimensions.

### MWeb / competitor reference

### Likely files
Sources/SilkwebCore/MarkdownTable.swift; Sources/Silkweb/TableInsertSheet.swift.

## UX notes — silkweb-1.14 Pipe-table insertion
Foundation: `.team/ux/_design-system.md` (§5 sheet conventions, §6: Format ▸ Insert Table… ⌃⌘T). The entry goes in the Format menu after Shift Left, and in the editor context menu's Format submenu. It's disabled unless the editor is focused and editable.

### Sheet (`TableInsertSheet`, about 360pt wide, 20pt padding, `Form` with `.formStyle(.grouped)`)
```
Insert Table
  Columns      [ 3 ][−|+]        (1–20)
  Body rows    [ 2 ][−|+]        (1–100; header row always included)
  Alignment    [ Default | Left | Center | Right ]   (segmented, applies to all columns)

  ┌──────────────────────────────────────┐
  │ | Column 1 | Column 2 | Column 3 |   │  live source preview, monospaced
  │ |:---------|:---------|:---------|   │  `.caption`, 5 lines max, scrolls
  │ |          |          |          |   │
  └──────────────────────────────────────┘
                              [Cancel] [Insert]
```
- Steppers have editable numeric fields. Out-of-range typing clamps on commit and beeps. Insert is the default button (Return). Escape cancels.
- Alignment markers: Default `---`, Left `:---`, Center `:---:`, Right `---:`. Per-column alignment is edited in the source afterwards; that's acceptable for v1.
- Remember the last columns, rows and alignment in user defaults (tolerant).

### Insertion rules
- Insert at the caret. If there's a selection, replace it. *(No conversion of selected CSV/TSV in v1.)*
- Ensure a blank line before and after the table unless it sits at the document start or end.
- Header cells are "Column 1…N". Body cells are blank. Pad every column to the header width so the source is aligned and readable.
- After insertion, select "Column 1" so typing replaces it. The whole insertion is **one undo step** ("Undo Insert Table").
- Pipes typed into the generated header text are escaped as `\|` (Core `MarkdownTable`). The sheet doesn't accept cell text in v1 except the generated headers.

### States
Insert is disabled if a field holds a non-number. A read-only document disables the menu item.

### Accessibility
Steppers labeled "Columns" and "Body rows"; the segmented control "Alignment"; the preview "Table source preview" (static text). Fully keyboard operable.

### Out of scope
Graphical cell editing, Tab-to-next-cell navigation, adding rows or columns to an existing table, reformatting existing tables.

design:
## UX notes — silkweb-1.15 Local image and attachment insertion
Foundation: `.team/ux/_design-system.md` (§5.2 Editor Banner for errors, §6: Format ▸ Image… ⌃⌘I). Silkweb never uploads anything. Assets live in `.silkweb-assets/<document-id>/`, which is hidden from the sidebar.

### Entry points
1. **Paste ⌘V** when the pasteboard holds image data or image file URLs and **no plain text**. If plain text is present, text wins (1.5 behavior).
2. **Drop** image or other files from Finder onto the editor. The standard `NSTextView` drop caret shows the insertion point.
3. **Format ▸ Image… ⌃⌘I**: `NSOpenPanel` (images, multiple selection, prompt "Insert").

### What gets inserted
- Images: `![alt](relative/path)` on their own line (insert newlines as needed). Several items → one per line.
- Other files (PDF, zip…): copied the same way and inserted as `[report.pdf](relative/path)`.
- **alt** = the original filename without extension. For pasted raw images, the file is named `image-20261001-104215.png` (PNG for raster pastes) and alt = "image".
- After insertion, **select the alt text** of the (last) image so the user can type a description immediately.
- URL path: relative from the document's folder to the asset. Percent-encode only spaces, parentheses and URL-reserved characters (`<`, `>`, `#`, `?`, `%`). Keep non-ASCII letters as literal UTF-8 so the source stays readable (`Ünïcode%20photo.png`, not `%C3%9C…`). Filename collisions in the asset folder get " 2", " 3" via `uniqueName`.

### Feedback
- Copying happens off-main. Insert the text only after the copy succeeds. If it takes more than 500 ms, show a small inline progress in the status bar: "Adding 3 files…".
- No success notification. The inserted text is the feedback.
- Editor shows the link as text only. Thumbnails are a follow-up; 1.18 Preview shows the image.

### Errors
Editor Banner: "Silkweb couldn’t add “photo.heic”." / reason. With multiple files, succeeded items are inserted and failures listed: "2 of 5 files couldn’t be added." with a **Details** button that shows a popover list.

### Undo
⌘Z ("Undo Insert Image") removes the inserted text in one step. **The copied asset file stays** on disk so Redo works and nothing is ever deleted implicitly. This is consistent with "no automatic asset garbage collection." *(Orchestrator: this resolves the acceptance item "optionally staged asset per design" as "keep".)*

### Accessibility
Encourage alt text by selecting it after insert. The Image… command is reachable from the menu and keyboard, so drag isn't required.

### Out of scope
Remote image download, inline image rendering in the editor, image resizing or width syntax, asset cleanup, dragging list documents into the editor to create links (follow-up).

Foundation: `.team/ux/_design-system.md` (§3 inspector, §4 tokens, §5.7 Inspector, §6: ⌘R, ⌘4, ⌘7). HTML structure and `sw-` class hooks come from 1.16 and 1.17. This ticket writes the original `preview.css`.

### View modes
- **Detail toolbar, trailing group:** a segmented control with three icon segments, Editor (`doc.plaintext`), Split (`rectangle.split.2x1`) and Preview (`eye`), with help tags "Editor", "Split Editor and Preview" and "Preview". To its right: the Outline toggle (`list.bullet.indent`, help "Show Outline"). 1.21 adds Info (`info.circle`) after it.
- **View menu:** "Show Preview" / "Show Editor" ⌘R (the title flips) toggles between Preview and the last non-preview mode. "Split Editor and Preview" ⌘4 is a checkmark item; turning it off returns to Editor. "Show Outline" ⌘7 is a checkmark item.
- The mode is per window and persisted. Switching never touches editor text, selection or undo.
- **Split:** editor left, preview right, in an `HSplitView`-style divider (thin system divider), 50/50 by default, ratio persisted, min 280pt per pane. If the detail column is narrower than 600pt, Split still works but panes shrink to their minimum and the inspector auto-hides first.

### Preview rendering
- `WKWebView` with JavaScript disabled for content, a content rule list blocking every non-`file:` load, and read access limited to the library root. Set `underPageBackgroundColor`, and don't draw the default white before the first load (no white flash in dark mode).
- Re-render 250 ms after the last edit, off-main, latest result only. Preserve the scroll position across reloads (restore by nearest heading anchor, falling back to scroll ratio).
- **Links:** `#anchor` scrolls. Relative `.md` links inside the library open that document (same as a list selection). `http(s)` opens in the default browser via `NSWorkspace`, and only on click. Everything else does nothing.

### `preview.css` (original; light/dark via WebKit system colors)
- `:root { color-scheme: light dark; }`, body `font: 16px/1.6 -apple-system`, `color: -apple-system-label`, background `-apple-system-text-background`. Content `max-width: 720px; margin: 0 auto; padding: 32px 40px 80px`.
- h1 2em/600, h2 1.5em/600, h3 1.25em/600, h4–h6 1em/600; margin-top 1.6em, margin-bottom 0.5em. No underlines on headings. h1 and h2 have no rules (calm look).
- Links `-apple-system-blue`, underline on hover only.
- `code` uses `ui-monospace` at 0.9em, background `-apple-system-quaternary-label` at low alpha (or `color-mix` with label at 8%), radius 4px, padding 0.1em 0.3em. `pre` has padding 12px 16px, radius 6px, the same fill, and `overflow-x: auto`.
- Blockquote: 3px left border `-apple-system-separator`, `padding-left: 1em`, `-apple-system-secondary-label`.
- Tables: `.sw-table-wrap { overflow-x: auto }`. Cells have a 1px `-apple-system-separator` border and 6px 12px padding. `th` is 600 weight with a quaternary fill. `.sw-align-*` sets text-align.
- `img { max-width: 100% }`. `.sw-remote-image` shows alt text in a 1px dashed separator box: "Remote image not loaded: <alt>".
- `.sw-raw-html` monospace in tertiary label. `.sw-blocked-link` uses secondary label with a dotted underline. `.sw-task` has no bullet and the checkbox is accent-tinted. `.sw-toc` sits in a quiet box (left border plus "Contents" pseudo-heading). `.sw-footnotes` uses a smaller 0.9em size.
- `.sw-empty::before { content: "Nothing to preview"; }` centered and tertiary.

### Outline (Inspector ▸ Outline)
- `.inspector` on the right, toggled with ⌘7 or the toolbar button. Header: the segmented "Outline | Info" control (Info arrives in 1.21; until then show just the title "Outline").
- Rows use Core `headings` (1.17): indent 12pt per level below the shallowest present, `.body` for levels 1–2, `.callout` secondary for 3+, single line truncated with a full-text tooltip.
- The **current section** (heading containing the editor caret, or the topmost visible heading in Preview mode) gets a 3pt accent bar on the leading edge and primary color text. It isn't a selection, so it doesn't fight keyboard focus.
- Click or Return on a row moves the editor caret to the start of that heading line and scrolls it to the top third (or the typewriter anchor, 1.27). In Split and Preview modes, it also scrolls the preview to the anchor. Focus goes to the editor (Preview mode: stays in the outline).
- Updates are debounced with rendering (250 ms).
- Empty: `ContentUnavailableView` (compact): `list.bullet.indent`, "No Headings", "Start a line with # to add a heading."

### Accessibility
Segmented items are labeled. The outline is a list with rows labeled "Heading level 2, Methods". The current section is announced as selected-ish via `accessibilityValue("current")`. The preview web content is reachable by VoiceOver natively.

### Out of scope
Scroll sync between editor and preview, find in preview, clickable task checkboxes, custom themes (1.24 covers font size only), floating or left-docked outline.

title: #19 Background library search index
description:
**Roadmap #:** 19 · **Scope:** M · **Priority:** P1

### User problem
10,000 notes cannot be searched synchronously on each keypress.

### Proposed behavior
Derived title/body index with incremental updates and cancellable queries; folder scope; rebuildable local persistence; no backend.

### MWeb / competitor reference
Full-text library search.

### Likely files
Sources/SilkwebCore/SearchIndex.swift, SearchQuery.swift.

### Constraints
Indexing off main thread; benchmark 10k-note fixture.
design:
## UX notes — silkweb-1.19 Background search index (Core-only)
Foundation: `.team/ux/_design-system.md` (§2: the feature is called **Search Library**; the panel is **Quick Open**). There is no UI here. 1.20 consumes this, so expose the data below rather than strings.

**Index state for UI:**
- `building(indexed, total)`: 1.20 shows a subtle footer under results: "Indexing library… 4,210 of 10,000". Searching is allowed meanwhile, with the note "Results may be incomplete while indexing."
- `ready`: nothing shown.
- `rebuilding(reason)` after a corrupt or old index: same as building. Never alert the user; the index is derived data.

**Result payload (per hit):** document ID, display name (no `.md`), folder path components (for the `Writing › Drafts` caption), modified date, match kind (`title` / `body`), and a snippet. The snippet is about 120 characters of body text around the first match, with match ranges given separately. Don't pre-bold; the UI styles ranges. Strip Markdown markers from snippets where cheap (`#`, `*`, `` ` ``), collapse whitespace, and add a leading/trailing "…" when truncated.

**Ranking (so UI and tests agree):** exact title > title prefix > title word-prefix > title substring > body match. Ties break by modified date (newest first), then name. **Quick Open** uses title-only ranking, plus "recently opened" boosting when the query is empty. Keep the recents list in Core, versioned and tolerant.

**Matching:** case- and diacritic-insensitive (`café` matches `cafe`). Multiple words are AND-ed. No query grammar (no quotes or operators) in v1, so treat those characters literally.

**Scope:** `library` or `folder(id, includeSubfolders: true)`. Tag filters (1.21) intersect later.

**Out of scope:** search UI, highlighting, query language.

title: #2 Safe folder/file mutation engine
description:
**Roadmap #:** 2 · **Scope:** M · **Priority:** P1

### User problem
Organizing notes must not overwrite or corrupt files.

### Proposed behavior
Core primitives for create/rename/move with collision handling, root containment, cycle prevention, and case-only rename edge cases on case-insensitive volumes; emit a change set for UI. No UI in this ticket; movement before link support affects unlinked text only.

### MWeb / competitor reference
External-folder create/rename/move/delete management.

### Likely files
Sources/SilkwebCore/LibraryMutations.swift; Tests/SilkwebCoreTests/LibraryMutationsTests.swift.

### Constraints
Atomic filesystem operations where applicable; never silent overwrite; collisions leave both originals intact.
design:
## UX notes — silkweb-1.2 Safe mutation engine (Core-only)
Foundation: `.team/ux/_design-system.md` (§2 vocabulary, §5 Inline Rename Field). There is no UI here. 1.6 (create/rename), 1.7 (move) and 1.8 (trash) display these errors verbatim, so define them once as typed errors with `LocalizedError` strings. `<kind>` is "folder" or "document". Names show without `.md`.

**Name validation** (a pure function the UI calls on every keystroke; returns the first failing rule):
| Rule | Message |
|---|---|
| Empty or whitespace only | "A name can’t be empty." |
| Contains `/` or `:` | "Names can’t contain “/” or “:”." |
| Starts with `.` | "Names can’t begin with a period." |
| Reserved (`.silkweb`, `.silkweb-assets`) | covered by the period rule |
| > 255 UTF-8 bytes (with extension) | "That name is too long." |
| Collides (case-insensitive on case-insensitive volumes) | "A <kind> named “<name>” already exists in “<folder>”." |

Trim leading and trailing whitespace before validating and committing. A case-only rename of the same item ("plan" → "Plan") is valid. Handle it with a two-step temp rename, not as a collision.

**Mutation errors** (shown in an alert with title + informative):
- Cycle: "“<folder>” can’t be moved into itself or one of its subfolders."
- Root: "The library folder itself can’t be moved or renamed here." / "Use Finder to rename the library folder."
- Outside root: "Silkweb can only move items within this library."
- Source vanished: "“<name>” no longer exists." / "It may have been moved or deleted in Finder."
- Filesystem failure: "“<name>” couldn’t be <renamed|moved|created>." / underlying `localizedDescription`.

**Unique-name helper:** `uniqueName(base, in folder)` → "Untitled", "Untitled 2", "Untitled 3" (space + number, no parentheses). 1.6 (New Document/Folder), 1.7 (Keep Both), 1.10 (import) and 1.11 (conflict copies) reuse it.

**Change set:** every mutation returns old/new relative paths plus stable IDs. The UI uses them to keep selection and expansion on the same item after the operation.

**Out of scope:** UI, link rewriting (1.7), Trash (1.8).

Foundation: `.team/ux/_design-system.md` (§2 names: **Search Library**, **Quick Open**; §5.1 empty states; §6: ⇧⌘F, ⇧⌘O). Result data and ranking come from 1.19. ### Search Library (content-column search field)
- `.searchable(placement: .toolbar)` on the content column, placeholder "Search Library". **Edit ▸ Find ▸ Search Library… ⇧⌘F** focuses it (placed below the 1.13 items after a separator).
- **Scope bar** (`.searchScopes`) appears while the field has text: **All Documents** | **“<selected folder>”**. The folder scope includes subfolders. Default = the selected folder, or All Documents if that's what is selected. 1.21 adds a tag filter that intersects.
- Debounce 150 ms. Each keystroke cancels the previous query.
- Results **replace** the document list (same list view, a different row layout):
```

Writing › Drafts · Oct 1            ← `.caption` tertiary
…we should ship the folder tree first and then…   ← `.subheadline` secondary, 2 lines, match in semibold
```
- The content subtitle reads "23 results". A footer shows the 1.19 indexing note when relevant ("Indexing library… 4,210 of 10,000 · Results may be incomplete").
- No results: `ContentUnavailableView.search(text:)`. With a folder scope, add a button **Search All Documents**.

- **Escape** in the field (or the field's clear button) clears the query and restores the previous list, selection and scroll position exactly.

- An in-window floating panel (child `NSPanel` or overlay), 560pt wide, horizontally centered, top edge 20% down the window. `.regularMaterial` background, 10pt corner radius, system shadow.
- Field: `.title3`, `magnifyingglass` leading, placeholder "Open a document by name". Focused on open.
- Up to 12 rows, 32pt each: `doc.text`, the title with matched characters semibold, and the path trailing in `.caption` tertiary. The first row is preselected.
- Empty query: a **Recent** header with the last 12 opened documents. Query: title ranking from 1.19.
- Keys: ↑/↓ (wraps), Return opens in the preview tab, **⌘Return** opens in a new pinned tab (1.26), Escape or a click outside closes and **restores focus to the previous first responder**. ⇧⌘O again closes it.
- Opening selects the document's folder in the sidebar and the row in the list, so context is visible.
- No matches: a single row "No documents named “xyz”" (secondary, not selectable).
- Disabled when no library is open.

### Accessibility
The panel is a dialog labeled "Quick Open". The result count is announced on change ("5 results"). Rows are labeled "<title>, in <path>". The search scopes are a labeled segmented control.

### Out of scope
Query grammar or operators, searching inside Quick Open by content, regex, search history, saved searches.

## UX notes — silkweb-1.21 Tags as a second organization axis
Foundation: `.team/ux/_design-system.md` (§2: **Tag**; §3 sidebar TAGS section; §5.3 Inline Rename Field; §5.7 Inspector; §6: ⌘8 Show Document Info). **Owner decision:** tags live only in the `.silkweb` sidecar index and are never written into `.md` text or front matter.

### Surfaces
1. **Sidebar TAGS section** below the folder tree, hidden until at least one tag exists. Rows: `tag`, the name, and a count badge (1.9 badge style; documents carrying the tag, library-wide). Natural sort. Selecting a tag shows all documents with that tag across the library, behaving like All Documents filtered by the tag. The list title is the tag name, with subtitle "9 documents".
2. **Tag filter in a folder:** a content-toolbar `Menu` button `tag` (help "Filter by Tag") after the Sort button. It lists tags with checkmarks; selecting several means documents must have **all** of them. Active filters show as a 28pt filter bar at the top of the list (shared with the 1.9 "Including subfolders" bar; stack both if needed): "Tagged: [research ✕] [draft ✕]" plus a **Clear** button. Filters intersect with the folder, Include Subfolders, and Search Library queries (1.20).
3. **Inspector ▸ Info** (⌘8 or toolbar `info.circle`, next to Outline): segmented "Outline | Info". The Info pane, top to bottom: **Tags** token field, then Location (`Writing › Drafts`, click = Reveal in Finder), Created, Modified, and Words/Characters (from 1.25 when available). Caption under Tags in `.caption` tertiary: "Tags are saved in this library’s Silkweb index, not in the document file."
4. **List context menu ▸ Tags** submenu: existing tags with checkmarks (mixed state "–" for multi-selection), then "Edit Tags…" (opens Info with the token field focused).

### Tag editing (token field, `NSTokenField` bridge)
- Placeholder "Add tags". Autocompletes existing tags case-insensitively after one character. Return, comma or Tab commits a token. Delete or Backspace on a selected token removes it.
- Normalization: trim whitespace, collapse internal runs of spaces, max 64 characters, commas not allowed (they're the separator). Uniqueness is case-insensitive: typing "Research" when "research" exists uses the existing tag.
- With a multi-selection, the token field shows the tags common to all documents. Adding applies to all; removing removes from all.
- Each change is one undo step: "Undo Add Tag" / "Undo Remove Tag".

### Tag management (sidebar tag row context menu)
- **Rename Tag…** uses the inline rename field. Renaming to an existing name asks: "A tag named “research” already exists." / "Merge “Research Notes” into “research”? Documents with either tag will have “research”." Buttons: **Merge** (default), **Cancel**.
- **Delete Tag…** asks: "Delete the tag “draft”?" / "It will be removed from 12 documents. The documents themselves won’t change." Buttons: **Delete Tag** (destructive), **Cancel**. Undoable.
- A tag with zero documents disappears automatically.

### Empty states
- A tag selected with no remaining matches in a folder filter: `ContentUnavailableView` "No Matching Documents", "No documents in “Writing” have all of these tags." Button **Clear Filters**.
- Info pane with no document selected: "No Document Selected".

### Accessibility
Tag rows are labeled "<name>, tag, 9 documents". Tokens are announced by the token field natively. The filter bar chips are buttons labeled "Remove filter research".

Nested or hierarchical tags, tag colors, inline `#hashtags`, writing tags into front matter, drag-to-tag.

title: #22 Self-contained HTML export
description:
**Roadmap #:** 22 · **Scope:** M · **Priority:** P2

### User problem
Recipients need a readable document without Silkweb installed.

### Proposed behavior
Export one HTML file with print/read styling and embedded supported images; deterministic encoding; clear missing-asset errors; destination picker; never silently overwrite.

### MWeb / competitor reference

### Likely files
Sources/SilkwebCore/HTMLExport.swift; Sources/Silkweb/ExportCommands.swift.

design:
## UX notes — silkweb-1.22 Self-contained HTML export
Foundation: `.team/ux/_design-system.md` (§5.5 Alerts, §6: File ▸ Export ▸ HTML… ⇧⌘E). This shares the **Export** submenu and the missing-image preflight with 1.23 (PDF), so build the preflight as one reusable piece.

### Entry point
**File ▸ Export ▸ HTML… ⇧⌘E** (submenu order: HTML…, PDF…) in the group after Reveal in Finder. Also the document list context menu ▸ Export ▸ HTML…. Disabled with no single document selected or open.

### Flow
1. Flush the document's save (1.5).
2. **Preflight images** (Core `HTMLExport`, off-main). If any local image is missing, show an alert. Title: "2 images couldn’t be found." Informative: list up to 5 names (“diagram.png”, “photo.jpg”), then "and 3 more". Then: "The exported file will show their descriptions instead." Buttons: **Export Anyway** (default), **Cancel**.
3. `NSSavePanel`: default name "<document name>.html", directory = last export folder (remembered), else ~/Documents. Prompt "Export". The panel's built-in "already exists. Do you want to replace it?" confirmation is the explicit overwrite guard, so we never write over a file without it.
4. Write atomically. **Success shows nothing.** It matches Mac convention, and the file is where the user chose.
5. Failure: alert "“plan” couldn’t be exported." / reason.

### Output design
- A single `.html` file: `<!doctype html>`, `<meta charset="utf-8">`, `<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width">`, `<meta name="generator" content="Silkweb">`, and `<title>` = document name.
- Inline the **same stylesheet as preview (1.18)**, but replace WebKit-only `-apple-system-*` colors with portable equivalents. Light values: text `#1f1f1f`-ish near-black, background white, separators light gray. Include a `@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark)` block with matching dark values so the file looks right in any browser. This is the one place hex values are allowed, because the output leaves the app.
- Font stack: `-apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif`; code uses `ui-monospace, Menlo, Consolas, monospace`.
- Images are embedded as `data:` URIs. Missing images render via the `.sw-remote-image`-style dashed box with alt text. Remote `http(s)` images are left as links and not fetched. Note it in the dashed box: "Image not included: <alt>".
- No scripts. Internal `#anchors` and the TOC work. Relative `.md` links stay as written.

### Accessibility
Output keeps semantic HTML, `lang` set from the system language, alt text, and the TOC `nav` aria-label.

### Out of scope
Batch or folder export, website generation, choosing themes, Copy as HTML, PDF (1.23).

## UX notes — silkweb-1.23 Print and save a single document as PDF
Foundation: `.team/ux/_design-system.md` (§6: Print… ⌘P, Page Setup… ⇧⌘P, Export ▸ PDF… ⌥⌘P). This is consistent with 1.22: the same Export submenu, the same missing-image preflight alert and copy, and the same last-export-folder memory.

### Entry points
- **File ▸ Page Setup… ⇧⌘P** and **File ▸ Print… ⌘P** at the bottom of the File menu (standard position).
- **File ▸ Export ▸ PDF… ⌥⌘P** (second item after HTML…).
- All are enabled only when exactly one document is open. Otherwise they're disabled, not hidden.

### Print flow
1. Flush the save, then run the shared image preflight (the 1.22 alert; buttons **Print Anyway** / **Cancel** for print, **Export Anyway** / **Cancel** for PDF).
2. Render the same Core HTML as preview into an offscreen `WKWebView` with `print.css` and run `NSPrintOperation` with the **standard print panel** (system PDF menu included). Show the panel's preview thumbnails; no custom accessory view in v1.
3. Header and footer: use the system print header/footer (title + date + page numbers) controlled by the panel's checkbox. Default on.

### Export ▸ PDF… flow
`NSSavePanel` (default "<name>.pdf", prompt "Export", built-in replace confirmation) → `NSPrintOperation` with save-to-file disposition and **no print panel**. The system progress sheet appears for long documents. Success is silent. Failure: "“plan” couldn’t be exported as PDF." / reason.

### `print.css` (original; always light, regardless of appearance)
- Page margins 18mm (top and bottom) and 16mm (sides) via `@page`. Body 11pt/1.5 system font, black on white. Content full width (no 720px cap).
- Headings: `break-after: avoid`. `h1` and `h2` use `break-before: auto` (no forced page breaks).
- `pre`: `white-space: pre-wrap; word-break: break-word;` 9pt monospace, light gray background (prints fine in grayscale), `break-inside: avoid` for blocks under about 15 lines.
- Tables: full width, 9.5pt, 0.5pt gray borders, `thead { display: table-header-group }` so headers repeat on each page, rows `break-inside: avoid`. Wide tables wrap cell text instead of clipping.
- Images: `max-width: 100%; break-inside: avoid`.
- Links print as text only; no URL suffixes in v1. The TOC prints as a list without page numbers.
- Task checkboxes render as ☐/☑ glyphs so they survive print.

### States
Rendering takes more than 300 ms → the system print progress UI is enough; no custom spinner. No network requests (same content rule list as 1.18).

### Accessibility
Standard panels. Exported PDFs carry the document title as metadata (`NSPrintInfo` job title).

### Out of scope
Multi-document books, custom PDF themes, cover pages, page-numbered TOC, PDF outline/bookmarks.

- [ ] Local images referenced by the document appear in the PDF; no network requests are made while rendering
- [ ] Export as PDF asks for a destination and never silently overwrites an existing file

## UX notes — silkweb-1.24 Writing and appearance settings
Foundation: `.team/ux/_design-system.md` (§4 editor typography defaults, §6: Settings… ⌘,, Bigger/Smaller/Actual Size ⌘+/⌘−/⌘0). This feeds the `EditorStyle` introduced in 1.5 and the preview CSS variables from 1.18.

### Settings window (SwiftUI `Settings` scene)
A `TabView` with toolbar-style tabs: **Editor** (`textformat`), **Preview** (`eye`), **Appearance** (`circle.lefthalf.filled`). Width 500pt, height fits content. Use `Form` with `.formStyle(.grouped)`. Changes apply **live**. There's no Apply/OK. Each tab ends with a trailing **Restore Defaults** button (restores that tab only).

**Editor tab**
| Label | Control | Default / range |
|---|---|---|
| Font | Picker: System, Serif (New York), Monospaced (SF Mono), Custom… | System |
| Custom… | opens `NSFontPanel`; the picker then shows the chosen family name | — |
| Size | numeric field + stepper, "pt" suffix | 15 (10–32) |
| Line height | Picker: 1.2, 1.35, 1.5, 1.75, 2.0 | 1.5 |
| Text width | Picker: Narrow (600 pt), Medium (720 pt), Wide (900 pt), Full Width | Medium |
| Indent with | Picker: 2 Spaces, 4 Spaces, Tab | 4 Spaces |
| Spelling | Toggle "Check spelling while typing" | on |
| Substitutions | Toggle "Use smart quotes and dashes" | off |
Below the table: a **Sample** box, 80pt tall, rendered with the current editor style and 1.12 styling: "## A heading" + "Some **bold** text and `code`." This is the live preview of the settings. 1.27 adds a **Writing Modes** section to this tab.

**Preview tab**
| Label | Control | Default |
|---|---|---|
| Font | Picker: System, Serif (New York) | System |
| Size | stepper | 16 (12–24) |
| Line breaks | Radio group: "Join lines in a paragraph (standard Markdown)" / "Treat every line break as a new line" | Join |

**Appearance tab**
- "Appearance": segmented control **System | Light | Dark**, default System. Sets `NSApp.appearance`; the editor, preview and export dialogs follow.
- Static caption: "Silkweb uses your system accent color. Change it in System Settings › Appearance." No accent picker, per the design system.

### Shortcuts tied to settings
**View ▸ Bigger ⌘+, Smaller ⌘−, Actual Size ⌘0** change the editor size in 1pt steps within range. This is a temporary per-window zoom on top of the Settings size. **Actual Size** returns to the Settings value, and the zoom doesn't rewrite the preference. *(Orchestrator: confirm per-window temporary zoom.)*

### Behavior
- Applying a style never replaces text storage (keep the selection, scroll and undo). Re-layout only.
- Preview updates via CSS variables (`--sw-font-size`, `--sw-font-family`) injected without a full re-render.
- Out-of-range values in older or edited preference files clamp to the nearest bound. Unknown fonts fall back to System with no alert.

### Accessibility
Every control has a visible label (Form rows). The font picker announces the family. The sample box is labeled "Editor sample text". Dynamic adjustments respect Reduce Motion (no animated re-layout).

### Out of scope
Custom themes and CSS, separate UI font, per-library settings, editor color customization, keyboard shortcut customization.

## UX notes — silkweb-1.25 Keyboard, accessibility completion and document statistics
Foundation: `.team/ux/_design-system.md` (§5.6 Status Bar, §6 shortcut map, §7 accessibility baseline). This ticket **audits** the shipped app against §6 and §7 and fixes gaps. It also introduces the Status Bar and word counts.

### Status Bar (new shared component)
- A 24pt strip at the bottom of the detail column, `.bar` material, top hairline `separatorColor`, 12pt horizontal padding, `.caption` secondary monospaced digits.
- **Leading:** "1,204 words · 6,830 characters". With a non-empty selection: "38 of 1,204 words · 212 of 6,830 characters".
- **Trailing:** reserved for the Focus/Typewriter chip (1.27) and transient progress (1.15 "Adding 3 files…").
- **View ▸ Show Status Bar ⌘/** (the title flips to Hide). On by default, persisted. It stays visible in Preview-only mode, since counts still apply.
- Click on the counts: a popover with Words, Characters, Characters (no spaces), Paragraphs and Reading time ("about 5 min", 230 wpm).

### Count definitions (Core `DocumentStatistics`, unit-tested)
- **Words:** Unicode word segmentation of the source text. Each CJK ideograph, kana run character or Hangul syllable block counts as one word. Markdown punctuation-only tokens (`#`, `-`, `*`, `|`, `>`, fences) aren't words. URLs inside `(…)` of links/images aren't counted. *(Orchestrator: confirm counting source text minus markup, rather than rendered text.)*
- **Characters:** grapheme clusters, including spaces and excluding line breaks.
- Debounce 300 ms after the last edit. Documents over 50k characters compute off-main. The selection count updates on selection change with the same debounce.

### Shortcut and menu audit (deliverable checklist)
1. Every command in §6 exists with exactly that equivalent. No duplicates (write a unit test over a Core `CommandCatalog` table if commands are declared there).
2. **Menu validation by focus:** Format and Find items need an editable editor focus. Rename, Move to Trash and Move To… need sidebar or list focus with a valid selection. Export, Print and Tags need one document. Disabled items stay visible.
3. Context-menu titles match the menu bar exactly ("Move to Trash", "Reveal in Finder").
4. Focus loop: Tab / ⇧Tab sidebar → list → editor → inspector. Go ▸ ⌥⌘1/2/3 work from anywhere, including from the find bar and banners.

### Accessibility audit (each surface)
- Sidebar row: "<name>, folder, 8 documents". List row (one element): "<title>, modified <date>[, in <path>][, tags: a, b]".
- All icon-only toolbar buttons: label + `.help` in menu wording. Segmented editor modes are labeled.
- Banners, move/trash results and import completion post `NSAccessibility` announcements.
- Drag alternatives: Move To… (1.7), Image… (1.15).
- Reduce Motion: no spring-load or expand animations; Typewriter scroll is instant.
- Increase Contrast: no custom colors means system handling applies. Verify no text uses `quaternaryLabelColor`.
- Write static or structural tests where possible (accessibility labels defined in one place, e.g. `AccessibilityLabels.swift`, unit-tested for non-empty strings).

### Out of scope
Custom shortcut editing, VoiceOver rotor customizations, goals or targets for word counts, the stats history.

title: #26 Document tabs and session restore
description:
**Scope:** L · **Priority:** P2 · **Product-owner request (2026-10-01)**

### User problem
The three-pane shell (#4) and single-document editor (#5) cannot keep multiple notes open, reuse a preview slot, or restore the last working set after quit—unlike MWeb’s tabbed editor workflow (`research.md` **Tabs/session**).

### Proposed behavior
- **Tab bar** in the editor pane of the main window: each tab binds one library document (stable ID from #1) with its own dirty buffer via `DocumentSession` / save coordinator (#3, #5).
- **Preview vs pinned:** one replaceable *preview* tab; selecting a document in the list opens it there unless that document is already open in another tab. First edit or double-click *fixes* the tab (pinned); pinned tabs persist across list selections until closed.
- **Tab chrome:** reorder (drag), close, **Close Others**, **Close Tabs to the Right**; **Cmd-W** closes the active tab (not the window when tabs remain—align with standard Mac tab semantics).
- **Navigation:** **Ctrl-Tab** and **Cmd-Shift-]** activate next tab (document shortcut collision matrix in #25; do not steal Cmd-R preview toggle, Cmd-O / Cmd-Shift-O open paths from #20, or find/replace keys from #13).
- **Session restore:** on launch, restore open tabs (pinned + preview state), active tab, and selected folder from versioned library/window metadata; decode tolerantly; drop entries whose files are missing; when a file was moved externally, rebind tab to the same stable document ID via library reconcile (#11) / move IDs (#7) when possible.
- **Moves:** when #7 moves or renames a document, open tabs follow the file path without orphan buffers.
- **Quit/close:** save coordinator flushes every dirty tab before tab close, window close, and app termination.

### MWeb / competitor reference
`research.md` **Tabs/session** (H/L2): replaceable preview tab; editing or double-click makes tab fixed; reorder/close subsets; reopen last session.

### Likely files
Sources/Silkweb/EditorTabBar.swift, TabbedEditorPane.swift, LibraryWorkspace.swift (list → tab routing), DocumentSession.swift, AppCommands.swift; Sources/SilkwebCore/WindowSessionMetadata.swift (or extend LibraryMetadata.swift) with tolerant Codable + tests in Tests/SilkwebCoreTests/WindowSessionMetadataTests.swift.

### Constraints
- Repo today is skeleton-only (`SilkwebApp.swift` placeholder; no tab or shortcut code yet)—implement on top of #4/#5 deliverables.
- Follow #5 autosave/debounce and flush-before-close; follow #7 move/link semantics for open documents.
- Session JSON must version and default missing keys; never block launch on stale session data.
- No per-keystroke library rescan (AGENTS.md performance rules).
design:
## UX notes — silkweb-1.26 Document tabs and session restore
Foundation: `.team/ux/_design-system.md` (§3 detail column, §4 `.bar` material, §6: ⌘T, ⌘W, ⇧⌘W, ⌃⇥ / ⇧⌘], ⌃⇧⇥ / ⇧⌘[, ⌥⌘W). Tabs are **inside the detail column** of the one library window. They're not `NSWindow` tabs, which would create separate windows with separate sidebars.

### Tab bar
- Sits directly under the window toolbar, above any Editor Banner and the find bar. 28pt tall, `.bar` material, bottom hairline `separatorColor`.
- **Shown when 2 or more tabs are open.** With a single tab (or none) it's hidden, so a single-document workflow looks identical to before (Safari-like). *(Orchestrator: confirm; alternative is "always show".)*
- Tabs share width equally, min 110pt, max 220pt. Beyond the available width the bar scrolls horizontally, with an overflow `chevron.down` menu at the trailing edge listing all tabs.
- **Tab anatomy:** a centered `.callout` title (document name, middle-truncated) and a 16pt close button on the leading side. The close button appears on hover and on the active tab. When the document is dirty, a `•` replaces the ✕ until hovered (Xcode/Safari convention).
- **Active tab:** `controlBackgroundColor` fill and primary text. **Inactive:** no fill and secondary text. Hover adds a subtle `quaternarySystemFill`.
- **Preview tab:** title in *italic* with tooltip "Preview — edit or double-click to keep this tab open". Only one preview tab exists at a time.
```
| ✕ plan for q3 | • outline | *meeting notes* |          ⌄ |
   active          dirty        preview (italic)
```

### Behavior
- **List selection** (single click, arrow keys, Search or Quick Open Return): if the document is already open in any tab, activate it. Otherwise, load it into the preview tab, creating one if needed and placing it right of the active tab.
- **Pinning:** the first edit, a double-click on the list row, a double-click on the tab, or the tab context item **Keep Open** turns the preview tab into a normal tab (title no longer italic).
- **⌘T / File ▸ Open in New Tab** (and ⌘Return in Quick Open, the list context menu's "Open in New Tab") opens the selection as a pinned tab.
- **Reorder** by dragging within the bar; a 2pt accent insertion indicator shows the gap. Dragging out of the window or between windows is out of scope.
- **Close:** ⌘W closes the active tab, then activates the tab to its **right**, else the left. With no tabs, ⌘W closes the window. ⇧⌘W always closes the window. Middle-click closes a tab.
- **Tab context menu:** Close Tab (⌘W) · Close Other Tabs (⌥⌘W) · Close Tabs to the Right · — · Keep Open (preview tab only) · Reveal in Library (selects in the sidebar and list) · Reveal in Finder.
- **Cycling:** Window ▸ Show Next Tab ⌃⇥ / ⇧⌘], Show Previous Tab ⌃⇧⇥ / ⇧⌘[ (wraps). ⌘1–9 are intentionally not tab selectors (§6).
- **Sync:** activating a tab selects its folder in the sidebar and its row in the list, unless a search is active (then only the editor changes).

### Saving
Closing a tab flushes its save. If the save fails, the tab stays open, becomes active, and shows the 1.5 banner. With tabs, switching documents no longer blocks on save failures: each tab keeps its own buffer, undo stack, caret and scroll.
Quit or window close flushes all tabs. Failures use the 1.5 quit alert.

### Session restore (silent)
Restore the open tabs (order, pinned/preview), active tab, caret and scroll per tab, selected folder, and view mode. Missing documents are dropped silently. Moved documents rebind by ID (1.7/1.11). Stale session data never blocks launch or shows an alert.

### Accessibility
The tab bar is an `AXTabGroup`. Tabs are radio-button-like with the label "<name>[, edited][, preview]". Close buttons are labeled "Close <name>". All tab commands are in the Window menu, so the mouse is never required.

### Out of scope
Multiple windows or libraries, tab tear-off, split editor groups, pinned/sticky tab icons, reopening closed tabs (⇧⌘T reserved for later).

## UX notes — silkweb-1.27 Focus and typewriter writing modes
Foundation: `.team/ux/_design-system.md` (§4 semantic colors, §5.6 Status Bar, §6: Focus Mode ⌃⇧⌘F, Typewriter Mode ⌃⇧⌘T). This builds on 1.12 styling, 1.24 settings, and the 1.25 status bar.

### Entry points
- **View ▸ Focus Mode ⌃⇧⌘F** and **View ▸ Typewriter Mode ⌃⇧⌘T**: checkmark items in their own group after the editor-mode items (Show Preview / Split / Outline). They're enabled when the editor is visible (Editor or Split mode) and disabled in Preview-only mode, where the state is kept.
- There are **no toolbar buttons**, to keep chrome minimal. While either mode is on, the trailing side of the Status Bar shows a borderless chip: "Focus", "Typewriter" or "Focus · Typewriter". It's `.caption`, accent-colored, and clicking it opens a menu with both toggles. This is the visible way out of the mode.
- The state is per window and persisted. New windows start with the last-used state.

### Focus Mode visuals
- Non-active text is dimmed by applying **temporary attributes** (`NSLayoutManager.addTemporaryAttribute(.foregroundColor)`) set to the run's existing color at about 30% opacity (blend toward `textBackgroundColor`). This never touches text storage, undo or 1.12 attributes. Markers already tertiary drop proportionally.
- **Active region**, per setting: **Paragraph** (default; a blank-line-delimited block, so a list item or a fenced code block counts as one unit) or **Sentence** (`enumerateSubstrings(.bySentences)` within the paragraph). A selection spanning several regions activates all of them.
- Updates on selection change, coalesced once per run loop, for the visible glyph range plus one screen of overscan only. No animation: the change is instantaneous, which avoids flicker while typing.
- It works in light and dark mode automatically because opacity is relative to the semantic colors.
```
GOOD                                   BAD
 dim  The previous paragraph…           Blurring or hiding text: unreadable
 FULL The one I'm typing in now|        Dimming to <20%: lost context, fails contrast
 dim  The next paragraph…               Dimming headings differently: inconsistent
```

### Typewriter Mode behavior
- Keeps the **caret line** at the anchor: Upper Third (33%), **Middle (50%, default)** or Lower Third (66%) of the visible editor height.
- Re-anchors on text input and keyboard caret movement only. Mouse or trackpad scrolling is free and doesn't fight the user, and a mouse click doesn't jump the view; the next keystroke re-anchors.
- Scrolling is instant (no animation; this also satisfies Reduce Motion). The 1.5 bottom inset already lets the last line reach the anchor. Add an equivalent top inset when on, so the first line can too.
- Find (1.13) and Outline (1.18) jumps land at the anchor instead of the top third.

### Settings (1.24 Editor tab, new section "Writing Modes")
| Label | Control | Default |
|---|---|---|
| Focus highlights | Segmented: Paragraph · Sentence | Paragraph |
| Typewriter position | Picker: Upper Third · Middle · Lower Third | Middle |

### Accessibility
Dimming is visual only: VoiceOver reads all text normally, and the menu items report their checked state. With Increase Contrast enabled, raise dim opacity to 55%. Focus and Typewriter don't change keyboard behavior.

### Out of scope
Full-screen "distraction-free" chrome hiding (use the system ⌃⌘F full screen plus the sidebar toggle), line-level or custom dim levels, typewriter sound effects.

title: Crash (stack overflow) when opening a document in the editor
description:
Reported by the product owner: opening a file in a library quits the app immediately.

Crash report ~/Library/Logs/DiagnosticReports/Silkweb-2026-10-01-100728.ips: EXC_BAD_ACCESS / SIGSEGV KERN_PROTECTION_FAILURE on the main thread = stack overflow from infinite recursion:
PlainMarkdownTextView.setFrameSize (MarkdownTextView.swift:128) -> layoutEditor() -> textContainer.containerSize = ... (:134) / textContainerInset = ... (:135) -> NSTextContainer setSize / NSTextView setTextContainerInset -> NSLayoutManager textContainerChangedGeometry -> view resized -> setFrameSize -> layoutEditor -> ... forever.

title: #3 Atomic document save coordinator
description:
**Roadmap #:** 3 · **Scope:** M · **Priority:** P1

### User problem
Interrupted or failed saves must not lose user writing.

### Proposed behavior
Serialized per-document writes with temp-file replace, revision token, recoverable draft on failure; dirty state clears only on successful commit.

### MWeb / competitor reference
Editable local notes and recovery-oriented workflow (implementation details U).

### Likely files
Sources/SilkwebCore/DocumentStore.swift, SaveCoordinator.swift; Tests/SilkwebCoreTests/SaveCoordinatorTests.swift with injected filesystem failures.

### Constraints
Atomic write temp + replace; never lose text on failure paths.
design:
## UX notes — silkweb-1.3 Atomic save coordinator (Core-only)
Foundation: `.team/ux/_design-system.md` (§5.2 Editor Banner). There is no UI here. 1.5 maps these states to UI, so expose them as an observable per-document state, not strings.

**Save state enum** (what the UI shows):
| State | UI in 1.5 |
|---|---|
| `clean` | nothing; window close button has no dirty dot |
| `dirty` (edited, save pending) | close-button dirty dot (`isDocumentEdited`) |
| `saving` | nothing new (avoid flicker); dot remains |
| `failed(error, attempt)` | Editor Banner (see below) and the dot remains |
| `conflict(diskRevision)` | handed to 1.11's conflict banner |

Never show a spinner for routine saves.

**Error copy** (`LocalizedError`), used in the banner as "Silkweb couldn’t save “<name>”." plus a reason line:
- Disk full: "There isn’t enough space on the disk."
- Permission: "You don’t have permission to write to “<folder>”."
- Volume gone: "The disk containing this library is no longer available."
- File vanished during save: route to 1.11 (external delete), not a generic error.
- Other: underlying `localizedDescription`.

Recovery is always implied, so the reason line ends with: "Your text is safe in this window."

**Recovery draft:** when a save fails, or at quit with unsaved text, write a draft under Application Support (not inside the library). Expose `pendingRecoveryDrafts()` so the app can show on next launch: "Silkweb recovered unsaved changes to 2 documents." with buttons "Review…" and "Later". The review UI is a follow-up. For v1, at minimum open each recovered draft in the editor as dirty.

**Revision token:** used by 1.11 to detect "changed on disk since load". No UI.

**Out of scope:** banners/alerts themselves (1.5), conflict UI (1.11).

title: Moves/undo fail when Finder adds .DS_Store; folder links lose trailing slash
description:

title: Library isn't reopened after a rebuild/update ('Can't Open Library — choose your library folder again')
description:
Reported by the product owner (screenshot): launching a new build shows 'Can't Open Library — Choose your library folder again to restore access.' every time.

Root cause (orchestrator): LibraryWorkspace stores the library location as a SECURITY-SCOPED bookmark (bookmarkData(options: [.withSecurityScope]) at LibraryWorkspace.swift:197; URL(resolvingBookmarkData:options:[.withSecurityScope]) at :107). Security-scoped bookmarks are bound to the app's code signature, and scripts/bundle_app.sh produces an ad-hoc-signed app whose code identity changes on every build (codesign identifier 'Silkweb-<cdhash>'), so each rebuild — and any future update — can't resolve the previous build's bookmark.

Fix: the app is not App-Sandboxed, so a security scope isn't needed. (1) Save a regular bookmark (no .withSecurityScope; e.g. [] or .minimalBookmark) PLUS the standardized path as a fallback; on launch resolve the bookmark without security scope, fall back to the saved path if resolution fails but the folder exists, refresh the stored bookmark when stale, and only show the error when the folder truly can't be found/read ('Library Not Found' / 'Can't Open Library'). (2) Migrate: an existing security-scoped bookmark in UserDefaults 'libraryBookmark' must still be tried, then replaced with the new format; users must not have to re-choose the folder more than once. (3) In scripts/bundle_app.sh, codesign ad-hoc with a stable identifier (codesign --force -s - -i com.silkweb.app build/Silkweb.app) so the code identity is consistent across builds. Keep startAccessingSecurityScopedResource calls harmless (call only when a scoped URL was actually resolved), so a future sandboxed build can opt back in. Put the resolve/fallback/migration decision logic in SilkwebCore and unit-test it.

description:
Reported by the product owner on build 47cda03: opening a new/empty document, the 'Start writing…' placeholder flickers/blinks continuously.

title: #4 Three-pane library shell
description:
**Roadmap #:** 4 · **Scope:** M · **Priority:** P1

### User problem
The app cannot navigate a library yet.

### Proposed behavior
Library root chooser, folder outline, direct-child document list, selection plumbing, read-only document placeholder; keyboard tree navigation; clear empty and error states. Usable shell before editor integration.

### MWeb / competitor reference
Category sidebar, document list, editor area layout.

### Likely files
Sources/Silkweb/SilkwebApp.swift, LibraryWorkspace.swift, FolderSidebar.swift, DocumentList.swift.

### Constraints
Thin app layer; scan via Core APIs from #1.
design:
## UX notes — silkweb-1.4 Three-pane library shell
Foundation: `.team/ux/_design-system.md` (§3 layout, §4 tokens, §5.1 empty states, §6 shortcuts). This ticket establishes the window that every later ticket plugs into, so build the structure exactly as specified even where later tickets fill it in.

### Entry points
- **First launch / no library** shows a Welcome view filling the whole window (no split view):
```
                 [books.vertical, 48pt, secondary]
                        Silkweb                    (.largeTitle)
           Write Markdown in folders you own.      (.title3, secondary)

   ┌──────────────────────────────┐  ┌──────────────────────────────┐
   │ [folder]  Open Folder in Place… │  │ [plus.rectangle.on.folder] New Library… │
   │ Use an existing folder of     │  │ Start an empty library in a   │
   │ Markdown files where it is.   │  │ new folder.                   │
   └──────────────────────────────┘  └──────────────────────────────┘
        To copy files in instead, use File › Import Folder Copy…   (.caption, tertiary)
```
  The two cards are large bordered buttons, 240×88, 16pt gap. "Open Folder in Place…" is the default (Return). The Tab key moves between them. This is an owner decision: both are offered, and Import Copy is in the File menu only (enabled once a library is open).
- **File ▸ Open Folder in Place… ⌘O**: `NSOpenPanel`, directories only, prompt "Open", message "Choose a folder to use as your Silkweb library. Documents stay where they are."
- **File ▸ New Library… ⌥⌘N**: `NSSavePanel`, prompt "Create", default name "Silkweb Library" in ~/Documents. Creates the directory and opens it.
- Silkweb remembers the last library (security-scoped bookmark) and reopens it on launch. One library per window. Multiple libraries are out of scope.

### Layout (when a library is open)
`NavigationSplitView` with widths per §3. Sidebar = `NSOutlineView` source list:
1. Section header **LIBRARY**.
2. **All Documents** (`doc.on.doc`): virtual. Lists every document recursively.
3. **Library root** row (`books.vertical`, directory name), expanded by default. Its children are the folders (`folder`), in natural order (`localizedStandardCompare`).
Content column: direct-child documents of the selected folder. Row = title (`.headline`, 1 line) + second line `.subheadline` secondary: modified date + first line of text, truncated. Row height about 44pt. Detail: read-only document text placeholder for now (1.5 replaces it). Use a plain selectable `Text` in the system body font, inside a scroll view with the §4 editor insets.

### States
| Where | State | Display |
|---|---|---|
| Sidebar | loading > 300 ms | small `ProgressView` + "Loading library…" in place of the tree; after 1 s append the count ("… 4,210 documents") |
| List | folder has no docs | `ContentUnavailableView`: `doc.text`, "No Documents", "This folder is empty." (1.6 adds a "New Document" button) |
| List | whole library empty | "No Documents Yet", "Create a document or folder to get started." |
| List | All Documents / nothing selected | nothing selected → "Select a Folder" |
| Detail | no selection | `doc.text`, "No Document Selected", "Select a document in the list." |
| Detail | multi-selection | `doc.on.doc`, "3 Documents Selected" (no actions yet) |
| Window | root missing | full-window `ContentUnavailableView`: `externaldrive.badge.questionmark`, "Library Not Found", "Silkweb can’t find “<name>”. It may have been moved, renamed, or be on a disconnected drive." Buttons: **Locate…** (open panel) and **Open Another Folder…** |
| Window | permission denied | `lock`, "Can’t Open Library", "Silkweb doesn’t have permission to read “<name>”." Button: **Choose Folder Again…** |

Never crash or show a blank window. An empty folder still shows in the tree.

### Keyboard
- In the sidebar: ↑/↓ move selection. → expands, or moves to the first child if already expanded. ← collapses, or moves to the parent. ⌥→/⌥← expand/collapse all descendants. Type-select by name.
- Tab / ⇧Tab cycles focus sidebar → list → detail. **Go ▸ Folders ⌥⌘1 / Documents ⌥⌘2 / Editor ⌥⌘3** jump focus directly. Add a **Go** menu between View and Window.
- In the list: ↑/↓, ⇧-extend, ⌘A select all. Return is reserved for Rename (1.6).
- Selection and expansion state persist per library (tolerant JSON). 1.26 later adds tabs to the session.

### Window chrome
- Title = selected document name, or else the folder name. `navigationSubtitle` = folder path relative to the library (`Writing › Drafts`).
- View menu includes the system sidebar toggle ⌃⌘S and toolbar ⌥⌘T.
- No custom toolbar items yet. 1.6, 1.9, 1.18 and 1.20 add them in the positions their notes specify.

### Accessibility
Sidebar rows: label "<name>, folder" (root: "<name>, library"; All Documents: "All Documents"). List rows read as one element: "<title>, modified <relative date>". Welcome cards are buttons whose label is the title and whose hint is the subtitle.

### Out of scope
Create/rename (1.6), drag and drop (1.7), counts and sorting (1.9; until then, list order is name A→Z), editing (1.5), tags section (1.21), multiple windows/libraries.

title: Preview is blank and images never show (page loaded outside WebKit read-access root)
description:
Product owner on 47cda03: preview 'just does not work' and images don't show.

Root cause (orchestrator, from code): PreviewView.Coordinator.load() writes the page HTML to FileManager.temporaryDirectory/SilkwebPreview-<UUID>/<UUID>.html (PreviewView.swift:61,95) and then calls web.loadFileURL(file, allowingReadAccessTo: root) with root = the LIBRARY folder (:106). WebKit only loads a file URL that is inside readAccessURL, so the page itself is refused -> blank preview, and no images. silkweb-1.18 QA could not run WebKit in the sandbox, so this was never observed.

Fix (engineer decides, preferred first):
1. Serve the preview through a custom WKURLSchemeHandler (e.g. silkweb-preview://page/<id> for the HTML and silkweb-preview://asset/<relative path> for images), resolving asset paths strictly inside the library root (reuse the 1.16 containment rules), with correct MIME types. No temp files, no broad file access, works for read-only libraries. Update HTMLRenderer/PreviewCoordinator so image src uses the scheme, and update the CSP (img-src silkweb-preview:) and content rule list accordingly. Links: #anchor scroll, relative .md -> open document, https -> open in default browser (decidePolicyFor).
2. Acceptable alternative: page file inside the library's .silkweb/preview/ (scanner-ignored) with allowingReadAccessTo: root, plus a temp-dir fallback for read-only libraries with readAccess on a common ancestor — only if 1 proves infeasible; explain why.
Keep JS disabled for page content, no network requests, debounced latest-result rendering. Also include the 1.18 follow-up: do not render/reload the preview while its pane is hidden (overlaps silkweb-1.39).

REQUIRED test — real WebKit, not code review: an app test that creates a temp library with a document containing a heading, a paragraph, a table and ![p](img/p.png) (a real 4x4 PNG written by the test), hosts the REAL PreviewView/WKWebView in an offscreen NSWindow, waits for navigation didFinish (timeout 10 s), then uses web.evaluateJavaScript (host-injected JS is allowed even with page JS disabled) to assert: document.querySelector('h1').textContent matches, the table exists, and document.images[0].complete && document.images[0].naturalWidth == 4. Also assert a remote https image is NOT loaded. If WebKit cannot run in the engineer/QA sandbox, the test must XCTSkip there with a clear message — the ORCHESTRATOR will run it unsandboxed and will verify it fails on 47cda03 and passes with the fix.
