title: #5 Native text editor with autosave
description:
**Roadmap #:** 5 · **Scope:** L · **Priority:** P1

### User problem
Users cannot write safely in the app.

### Proposed behavior
NSTextView bridge with Unicode/IME, undo/redo, plain-text paste, native spelling; debounced autosave and flush before selection change/close; save failures retain buffer and block silent loss.

### MWeb / competitor reference
Source-first Markdown editing with native Edit commands.

### Likely files
Sources/Silkweb/MarkdownTextView.swift, DocumentSession.swift, AppCommands.swift; Core tests for buffer/save scheduling where testable without AppKit.

### Constraints
Debounce saves; no main-thread library rescan per keystroke.
design:
## UX notes — silkweb-1.5 Native text editor with autosave
Foundation: `.team/ux/_design-system.md` (§4 editor typography, §5.2 Editor Banner, §6 Edit-menu shortcuts). This replaces the 1.4 read-only placeholder in the detail column.

### Layout
- `NSTextView` in an `NSScrollView` filling the detail column, background `textBackgroundColor`, text `labelColor`. The insertion point uses the accent color.
- Text container width = min(available width − 2×40pt, 720pt), centered. Top inset 24pt, bottom inset 50% of the viewport so the last line can scroll up comfortably (1.27 reuses this). Default font: system 15pt, line height 1.5× via paragraph style. 1.24 makes this configurable. Expose one `EditorStyle` value type now so 1.12, 1.24 and 1.27 extend it rather than re-plumbing.
- Empty document: a placeholder overlay at the caret line, "Start writing…", in `tertiaryLabelColor`. It disappears on the first character.
- Plain text only: `isRichText = false`, `importsGraphics = false` (1.15 handles images), `allowsUndo = true`, `usesFindBar = true` (prepared for 1.13).
- **Text-service defaults (Markdown-safe):** continuous spell checking on, grammar off, smart quotes off, smart dashes off, text replacement off, automatic link detection off, data detection off. All remain user-toggleable via the standard Edit ▸ Spelling and Grammar / Substitutions / Transformations / Speech submenus.

### Saving (no Save UI needed)
- Autosave is debounced to about 1 s after typing stops. Saves also flush on selection change, tab/window close, app deactivate and quit.
- **⌘S** = flush now. It shows no panel and no visual flash.
- **Dirty indicator:** set the window's `isDocumentEdited` (dot in the close button) while state ≠ clean. That's the only routine indicator, with no "Saving…" spinner.
- Paste (⌘V) and Paste and Match Style (⌥⇧⌘V) both insert plain text only.

### Failure states
- **Save failed:** an Editor Banner (systemOrange `exclamationmark.triangle.fill`). It reads "Silkweb couldn’t save “plan”. Your text is safe in this window." with the 1.3 reason as a secondary line, and buttons **Try Again** and **Save a Copy…** (`NSSavePanel`, any location). Typing continues. The next autosave retries automatically, and the banner clears itself on success.
- **Switching documents while the save fails:** the selection change is refused (the list selection reverts) and the banner pulses once (accessibility announcement). This stays until tabs (1.26) can hold the buffer.
- **Quit with an unsaved failure:** alert "Some changes couldn’t be saved." / "They’ll be kept as a recovery draft and offered the next time you open Silkweb." Buttons: **Cancel** (default), **Quit Anyway**.
- **Non-UTF-8 file:** opens read-only with the banner "This file isn’t UTF-8 text, so Silkweb opened it read-only." (info symbol, secondary color, no actions).
- **Recovered drafts on launch** (from 1.3): banner "Silkweb recovered unsaved changes to this document." with **Keep Recovered Text** and **Discard Recovered Text**. Discard asks for confirmation: "Discard the recovered text? This can’t be undone."

### Interaction details
- Selecting a document places the caret at the start the first time and restores the last caret/scroll position on revisit (in memory for this session; 1.26 persists it).
- Undo history is per document and cleared on switching documents (1.26 keeps it per tab).
- Focus: clicking a list row keeps focus in the list. Return… is Rename (1.6), so use ⌥⌘3 or Tab to enter the editor.

### Accessibility
The text view label is "Document text, <name>". Banners are announced. Standard VoiceOver text navigation works because it's a stock `NSTextView`. Avoid custom drawing that breaks it.

### Out of scope
Formatting and styling (1.12), find (1.13), images (1.15), tabs (1.26), version history.

title: #6 Create and rename from the library
description:
**Roadmap #:** 6 · **Scope:** M · **Priority:** P1

### User problem
An empty library offers no writing entry point.

### Proposed behavior
New folder, subfolder, and document in selection context; inline/editable filename with validation; Finder reveal; save before rename; stable selection after rename.

### MWeb / competitor reference
New note/category and external-folder context commands.

### Likely files
Sources/Silkweb/LibraryCommands.swift, FolderSidebar.swift, DocumentList.swift.

### Constraints
Reject empty, reserved, separator, and colliding names per research contract.
design:
## UX notes — silkweb-1.6 Create and rename from the library
Foundation: `.team/ux/_design-system.md` (§2 naming, §5.3 Inline Rename Field, §6 shortcuts). Validation strings come from 1.2. Reuse its validator and `uniqueName` helper; don't duplicate rules in the app.

### Target folder rule (used by every create command)
The **target** is the folder selected in the sidebar. If the sidebar selection is **All Documents** or a **Tag**, the target is the folder of the document selected in the list. If no document is selected either, the target is the library root. Context-menu commands target the clicked folder instead. 1.10 (import destination) and 1.15 reuse this rule.

### Commands and placement
| Command | Menu | Shortcut | Toolbar / context |
|---|---|---|---|
| New Document | File | ⌘N | content-column toolbar, leading-most: `square.and.pencil`, help "New Document" |
| New Folder | File | ⇧⌘N | sidebar bottom bar: `plus` pull-down → New Folder / New Document. Also context menu |
| Rename… | File | Return (sidebar/list focused only) | context menu |
| Reveal in Finder | File | ⌥⌘R | context menu |

**Folder row context menu** (clicked folder): New Document · New Folder · — · Rename… · Move To… (1.7) · Reveal in Finder · — · Move to Trash (1.8). Root row: same, minus Rename…, Move To… and Move to Trash (those are shown disabled, not hidden). **Document row context menu**: Open in New Tab (1.26) · — · Rename… · Move To… · Reveal in Finder · — · Move to Trash.

### New Folder flow
1. Create "Untitled Folder" (or "Untitled Folder 2", …) inside the target.
2. Expand the parent, scroll the new row into view, select it, and enter inline rename with the whole name selected.
3. Return commits and keeps the folder selected (the list shows its empty state). Escape keeps "Untitled Folder" (it already exists on disk) and exits rename.
4. ⌘Z (Edit ▸ Undo New Folder) removes it only if it's still empty. Otherwise the undo item is disabled.

### New Document flow
1. Flush the current document's save (1.5).
2. Create "Untitled.md" (or "Untitled 2.md", …) in the target, empty.
3. Select the row in the list (switch the sidebar to the target if it was All Documents) and open it in the editor.
4. Put the **list row** into inline rename with "Untitled" selected. Return commits and moves focus into the editor, caret at the start. Escape or Tab skips renaming and focuses the editor. *(Decision for Orchestrator: deliberate naming at creation, Finder-style, instead of auto-naming from the first line. This avoids silent file renames.)*
5. The file name never rewrites the document's first heading, and vice versa.

### Inline rename (sidebar and list)
- Start with Return on a selected row, a slow second click on the name of an already-selected row (about 0.5–1.5 s after the first click, Finder-like), or the Rename… context item.
- The field shows the base name only. The `.md` extension is never shown or editable. Leading and trailing whitespace is trimmed on commit.
- Validate live with the 1.2 rules. On failure the field gets a `systemRed` 1pt border and a popover below it shows the message (e.g. "A folder named “Drafts” already exists in “Writing”."). Return beeps. Escape reverts. Clicking away reverts silently when invalid and commits when valid.
- Case-only renames ("plan" → "Plan") must work.
- **Before renaming a dirty document:** flush the save first. If the save fails, abort the rename and show the 1.5 save banner.
- After commit: selection, expansion and any open editor/tab stay on the same item (by stable ID). Re-sort happens in place without the row jumping out of view (scroll to keep it visible). Window title updates.
- Disk failure: alert "“<old>” couldn’t be renamed." / reason. Button "OK" (single acknowledgement).
- Undo: Edit ▸ Undo Rename (⌘Z) restores the old name when the original name is still free.

### Empty-state actions
Update the 1.4 empty states: "No Documents" gets a **New Document** button. "No Documents Yet" gets **New Document** and **New Folder**.

### Accessibility
The rename field is labeled "Name". Validation messages are posted as accessibility announcements. The sidebar `plus` button is labeled "Add" with menu items "New Folder" and "New Document".

### Out of scope
Templates, auto-naming from content, Duplicate, renaming the library root (use Finder), creating documents with non-`.md` extensions.

title: #7 Folder and document moves with link planning
description:
**Roadmap #:** 7 · **Scope:** L · **Priority:** P1

### User problem
Folders and notes cannot be reorganized reliably.

### Proposed behavior
Internal drag/drop and Move To… share one transaction; prevent cycles and overwrites; preserve IDs; preflight supported relative Markdown link rewrites with staged rollback; report unsupported links.

### MWeb / competitor reference
Category drag management and external-folder tree (link-repair parity U).

### Likely files
Sources/SilkwebCore/MovePlan.swift, MarkdownDestinations.swift; Sources/Silkweb/MovePicker.swift; sidebar/list drop delegates.

### Constraints
Explicit bounded rewrite grammar; no silent merge on collision (cancel or unique name).
design:
## UX notes — silkweb-1.7 Folder and document moves with link planning
Foundation: `.team/ux/_design-system.md` (§3 sidebar, §5.4 Folder Picker, §6: Move To… ⌃⌘M). Drag-and-drop and Move To… run the **same** move transaction and the same preflight sheets. Only the way the destination is chosen differs.

### Drag sources
- **Document list rows**: single or multi-selection. Dragging an unselected row drags only that row. The drag image is the standard row snapshot with a count badge when there's more than one item.
- **Sidebar folder rows**, except the library root and All Documents.
- Internal pasteboard type only (stable IDs). Dragging out to Finder or other apps is out of scope; the drag isn't offered outside the window.

### Drop targets (sidebar only)
- **Valid:** any folder row or the library root ("drop on" only). Turn off between-row insertion indicators, because there is no manual ordering.
- **Invalid (no highlight, drop refused, drag snaps back):** the dragged folder itself, any of its descendants, the item's current parent (no-op), All Documents, and Tag rows. Tag drops are a follow-up.
- **Highlight:** the standard `NSOutlineView` drop highlight on the target row (accent rounded fill in source-list style). Only one row is highlighted at a time.
- **Spring-loading:** hovering over a collapsed folder for the system spring-loading delay (`NSEvent`/user default; roughly 0.5–0.7 s) expands it. Folders auto-expanded during the drag collapse again when the drag ends, unless the drop landed inside them. Pressing Space while hovering expands immediately (Finder convention).
- **Auto-scroll** when the pointer is within 24pt of the sidebar's top or bottom edge.
- Modifier keys are ignored in v1 (no Option-copy). The cursor always shows the move (arrow) cursor.

```
GOOD  ▾ Writing                 BAD   ▾ Writing
      ┃▓ Drafts ▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓┃  ← row        ─────────────── ← insertion line implies
        Archive                         Drafts          ordering we don't have
```

### Move To… (keyboard path, ⌃⌘M; File menu and context menus)
A sheet using the shared **Folder Picker** component, 440×480:
- Title: "Move “plan” To…" or "Move 3 Items To…".
- A filter field at the top, focused, with placeholder "Filter folders". Typing switches the outline to a flat list of matches with breadcrumb captions (`Writing › Drafts`) and highlights the matched text.
- Folder outline below, with the library root first. A **Recent** section (up to 3 recent destinations) sits above it when the filter is empty.
- Disabled rows: the items' current parent (caption "Current location"), the moved folders, and their descendants.
- ↑/↓ moves the selection, ←/→ collapses/expands, Return = **Move**, Escape = **Cancel**.
- Bottom-left **New Folder…** creates "Untitled Folder" inside the highlighted destination, puts it into inline rename, and selects it as the destination.
- Buttons: Cancel, **Move** (default; disabled until a valid destination is selected).
- 1.10 reuses this component with title "Import Into…" and button "Choose".

### Transaction and feedback
1. **Preflight** (off-main; show a sheet spinner only after 300 ms): name collisions, cycle/root checks (1.2 messages) and the link plan.
2. **Collision.** One alert per conflicting item, with a "Apply to All" suppression checkbox when there are several. Title: "An item named “plan” already exists in “Drafts”." Informative: "You can keep both by naming the moved item “plan 2”, or stop the move." Buttons: **Keep Both** (default), **Stop**. There is never a Replace or Merge option.
3. **Links.** Supported relative links are rewritten silently as part of the move. If unsupported links would break, show a sheet *before* moving. Title: "Some links might stop working". Body: "Silkweb can’t update these links automatically. They’ll stay as written." followed by a list (document › link text, ≤ 8 rows, scrolls). Buttons: **Move Anyway** (default), **Cancel**.
4. **Dirty documents** are saved first. If a save fails, the move doesn't start and the 1.5 banner shows.
5. **Execute.** Expansion is preserved. Moved items stay selected: if documents were moved out of the folder shown in the list, the list keeps its folder and the items simply leave it. If a folder was moved, the sidebar selects it in its new location and expands its new parent. Open editors and tabs follow by ID.
6. **Undo:** Edit ▸ Undo Move (⌘Z) reverses the last move, including link rewrites, while the paths are unchanged. If they changed, show an alert: "The move can’t be undone because items have changed since."
7. **Failure:** everything rolls back. Alert: "The items couldn’t be moved." / reason. "Nothing was changed."

### Accessibility
Move To… is the full accessible alternative to dragging. Picker rows are labeled "<name>, folder, <path>". Disabled rows are announced as "dimmed" with their caption. Drop targets announce the folder name via the standard outline view behavior.

### Out of scope
Copying (Option-drag), drag to/from Finder (Finder → library import is a follow-up to 1.10), dropping onto tags, manual ordering, dropping into the document list's background.

title: #8 Trash-based deletion
description:
**Roadmap #:** 8 · **Scope:** M · **Priority:** P1

### User problem
Deletion must be reversible.

### Proposed behavior
System Trash for documents and folders; descendant summary for nonempty folders; flush dirty state first; sensible selection after delete; no permanent-delete command.

### MWeb / competitor reference
Library Trash vs external system Trash (Silkweb: unified macOS Trash).

design:
## UX notes — silkweb-1.8 Trash-based deletion
Foundation: `.team/ux/_design-system.md` (§2: always "Move to Trash", never "Delete"; §5.5 Alerts; §6: ⌘⌫). "Trash" in Silkweb always means the macOS Trash. There is no in-app Trash list and no permanent-delete command anywhere.

### Entry points
- **File ▸ Move to Trash ⌘⌫**. The shortcut is active only when the sidebar or list has focus; in the editor ⌘⌫ keeps its text meaning (delete to line start). Also in folder/document context menus, last group.
- The menu title adapts: "Move “plan” to Trash", "Move 3 Items to Trash". The plain "Move to Trash" is shown disabled with no selection.
- Disabled for the library root and All Documents.

### When to confirm (Finder-like: Trash is recoverable)
| Selection | Confirmation |
|---|---|
| One or more documents | none; act immediately, undoable |
| Empty folder(s) | none |
| Any non-empty folder in the selection | alert (below) |

**Alert for non-empty folders:**
- Title: "Move “Projects” to the Trash?" For several items: "Move 4 items to the Trash?"
- Informative: "“Projects” contains 14 documents, 3 folders, and 6 other files. Everything inside will be moved to the Trash with it. You can restore it from the Trash in Finder." Omit zero counts. "Other files" covers images and attachments.
- If any contained document is open with unsaved changes, add: "Unsaved changes will be saved first."
- Buttons: **Move to Trash** (default, `.destructive` style) and **Cancel** (Escape). Counts come from Core `DeletionPlan`, computed off-main. Show a 300 ms-delayed spinner in the alert if counting is slow.

### Flow
1. Flush saves for every affected open document. **If a save fails**: show the alert "“plan” couldn’t be saved, so nothing was moved to the Trash." / "Your changes are still open in Silkweb." Button: **OK**. Never offer to discard text.
2. Trash the items via `FileManager.trashItem` (keep the resulting URLs for undo).
3. Close the tabs and editors of trashed documents silently.
4. **Selection after:** list → the next row below, else the row above, else the list empty state. Sidebar → the next sibling folder, else the previous one, else the parent. Focus stays in the same pane.
5. **Undo:** Edit ▸ Undo Move to Trash (⌘Z) puts items back from the Trash to their original paths if those are still free. If not, alert: "“plan” can’t be put back because an item with that name now exists." Also offer **Reveal in Trash**.
6. Sound: play the system "move to trash" sound only if it's easy (`NSSound(named: "dragToTrash")`); otherwise none. Optional.

### Errors
- Volume has no Trash (network or some external drives): "“plan” can’t be moved to the Trash." / "This disk doesn’t support the Trash. Silkweb never deletes documents permanently. Move it in Finder if you want to remove it." Buttons: **Reveal in Finder**, **OK** (default).
- Permission and other errors: "“plan” couldn’t be moved to the Trash." / reason. With partial failures, list failed items. Successfully trashed ones stay trashed and remain undoable.

### Accessibility
Alerts are standard and announced. Successful trashing posts the announcement "Moved 3 items to the Trash".

### Out of scope
In-app Trash browser, Empty Trash, permanent delete, Put Back from Finder (user does that in Finder; 1.11 rescans).

title: #9 Folder counts and document sorting
description:
**Roadmap #:** 9 · **Scope:** S · **Priority:** P1

### User problem
Users cannot scan or understand hierarchy size and document order.

### Proposed behavior
Direct document counts in sidebar; explicit include-subfolders recursive mode in list; natural folder ordering; name/created/modified sorts with stable tie-breakers; per-folder remembered sort preference.

### MWeb / competitor reference
Title/date/custom sorts (manual order excluded).

### Likely files
Sources/SilkwebCore/LibraryPresentation.swift; Sources/Silkweb/FolderSidebar.swift, DocumentList.swift.

### Constraints
Manual drag ordering deferred; disk filenames do not encode display order.
design:
## UX notes — silkweb-1.9 Folder counts and document sorting
Foundation: `.team/ux/_design-system.md` (§3 sidebar sketch, §4 monospaced digits, §6: Sort By ⌃⌥⌘1–3). Core `LibraryPresentation` owns the ordering and counts. The views only render them.

### Sidebar counts
- Each folder row shows its **direct** document count as a trailing badge (SwiftUI `.badge` / `NSTableCellView` trailing label): `.caption`-sized, secondary, monospaced digits, with a thousands separator ("1,204").
- **Zero shows nothing** (no "0" badge), so the sidebar stays quiet.
- **All Documents** shows the total. The library root shows its direct root documents.
- Tooltip on a folder row: "8 documents · 23 including subfolders". The recursive total appears only in the tooltip and the accessibility value, never as the badge, so users never confuse the two numbers.
- Counts update after create, move, trash or rescan, without animation jitter (no row reloads, just the badge).

### Folder order in the sidebar
Natural order (`localizedStandardCompare`: "Chapter 2" before "Chapter 10"), case-insensitive. It isn't user-configurable in v1.

### Document sorting (list)
- **Content toolbar:** a `Menu` button with `arrow.up.arrow.down`, help "Sort By", to the right of New Document. Its menu:
```
Sort By
 ✓ Date Modified        ⌃⌥⌘2
   Date Created         ⌃⌥⌘3
   Name                 ⌃⌥⌘1
 ───────────
 ✓ Newest First   /  Oldest First      (dates)
   A to Z         /  Z to A            (name)
 ───────────
   Include Subfolders
```
- The same items appear in **View ▸ Sort By** and **View ▸ Include Subfolders**.
- The direction labels change with the key: "Newest First / Oldest First" for dates, "A to Z / Z to A" for Name. Never say "Ascending".
- Choosing a new key resets the direction to that key's natural default: dates → newest first, Name → A to Z.
- **Default for every folder:** Date Modified, Newest First. *(Orchestrator: confirm the default; a writing-library convention.)*
- Tie-breaker: name (natural), then relative path. The order must be deterministic.
- Remembered **per folder** (keyed by folder ID, versioned metadata, tolerant decode). All Documents and each tag keep their own preference. A new folder starts with the default, not the parent's setting.
- The second line of the row shows the date matching the sort key: "Created Oct 1, 2026" when sorted by created, otherwise the modified date. Relative formatting: time today ("10:42 AM"), "Yesterday", weekday within 7 days, else a short date.

### Include Subfolders
- Off by default, remembered per folder. When on:
  - Each row gets a third line, a `.caption` tertiary path relative to the selected folder (`[folder] Drafts › 2026`). Omit it for direct children.
  - A slim header bar (`.bar`, 28pt) at the top of the list reads "Including subfolders · 23 documents" with a trailing borderless button **Show Only This Folder**, so the mode is never invisible.
- The content subtitle always shows the visible count: "12 documents" / "23 documents (with subfolders)".
- All Documents is inherently recursive, so the toggle is hidden (disabled in View) there.

### Accessibility
Folder row value: "8 documents, 23 including subfolders". The sort menu button is labeled "Sort By, Date Modified, Newest First" (current state in the label). The header bar is a labeled group.

### Out of scope
Manual drag ordering, sorting folders by date, sorting by size or tag, column/table view.

title: Epic — Silkweb v2: post-v1 roadmap
description:
## Summary

Post–Core v1 features and product-owner priorities for Silkweb: **custom HTTP integrations** (image upload + send document) first, then research.md **Later** items (rendering, export, organization, editor, capture/safety, customization, migration).

**Principles (carry from v1):** offline-first default; **no network** unless the user configured an integration and explicitly triggered it (or enabled auto-upload); no telemetry; timeouts and cancellation; secrets in Keychain; versioned tolerant JSON for non-secret persistence; `./scripts/build.sh` + tests per issue.

**Build order:** Section A (integrations) is P1 and should land before most Section B work that assumes preview/export maturity. v2 issues may depend on v1 (`silkweb-1.x`) tickets — those edges are recorded so nothing is *ready* before its foundation.

## Section A — Custom HTTP integrations (P1, first)

MWeb reference (bundled help/strings): **Custom** image-upload service with API URL, POST file field name, extra POST headers/body fields, Response URL Path (JSON key path) with optional URL prefix/suffix; local images POST on paste/drop or “copy with upload”; links rewritten to returned URL; upload history. Silkweb matches that behavior **and** supports sending whole documents via the same integration model.

Four dependent tickets: (1) Core definitions + Keychain, (2) settings UI + test request, (3) custom image upload, (4) send document to integration.

## Section B — Remaining Later roadmap

One ticket each (split only when too large): math (LaTeX), Mermaid, code highlighting + optional line numbers, editor↔preview scroll sync, fuller CommonMark conformance; ePub, DOCX, RTF/rich copy, rendered image export, folder→PDF compile, TextBundle; manual document ordering, pin, backlinks panel, in-app Trash browser, advanced search syntax; HTML→Markdown paste, inline image display modes, insert date/time, list renumbering, graphical table editor; Quick Note, scheduled backups, version history; custom theme/CSS, per-text-service settings, preferences import/export; clean-room MWeb Markdown-export import.

## Explicitly NOT planned (no tickets)

Blog publishing services; vendor-specific image hosting (use generic custom integration); static-site generation; cloud sync; iOS app.

title: Custom HTTP integrations — definitions and secure storage (Core)
description:
**Roadmap:** v2-A1 · **Scope:** L · **Priority:** P1

### User problem
Users need configurable HTTP endpoints for image hosting and document publishing without vendor lock-in or plain-text secrets on disk.

### Proposed behavior
Named integrations: POST method; URL (HTTPS default; HTTP only with per-integration explicit toggle); configurable headers and body fields; request format multipart/form-data, JSON, or application/x-www-form-urlencoded; template placeholders (`{{title}}`, `{{markdown}}`, `{{html}}`, `{{folderPath}}`, `{{tags}}`, `{{filename}}`, `{{createdAt}}`, `{{modifiedAt}}`); response mapping (JSON path → returned URL / remote ID, optional prefix/suffix). Secret header/body values stored in macOS Keychain, never in plain JSON or exported settings. Versioned tolerant JSON for non-secret parts. Pure request building + response parsing in SilkwebCore; fully unit-tested with stub `URLProtocol` (no real network in tests).

### MWeb / competitor reference
MWeb Custom image-upload service (API URL, file field, extra POST headers/body, Response URL Path, prefix/suffix); upload on paste/drop and copy-with-upload (Silkweb adds document send with same model).

### Likely files
Sources/SilkwebCore/IntegrationDefinition.swift, IntegrationRequestBuilder.swift, IntegrationResponseParser.swift, KeychainSecretStore.swift; Tests/SilkwebCoreTests/IntegrationRequestBuilderTests.swift, IntegrationResponseParserTests.swift.

### Constraints
No outbound network in Core tests; no telemetry; document no network entitlement usage until user-triggered flows land in App. Note App Sandbox `com.apple.security.network.client` if the app is later sandboxed.
